hypotheses.claim: A relation sigil with compact @name and quoted @"arbitrary identity" forms can eliminate the observed identifier/operator lexical ambiguity, preserve arbitrary relation identity, and remain close to current G9 surface cost without semantic redesign.
evidence: 20k deterministic fuzz with zero identity failures
counterhypotheses: strict generic relation(quoted_id,lhs,rhs) is operationally superior despite higher surface cost
declared contextual bare-infix relations outperform both strict lexical candidates
hypotheses.falsifier: Full admitted-corpus parser/roundtrip and reader benchmarks show semantic drift, ambiguity, worse diagnostics/repair, or a material reader/token advantage for a competing candidate.

hypotheses.claim: Open relation names belong in the typed symbol/resolution layer after lexical disambiguation; parser acceptance must not implicitly mint semantics for unknown relation names.
hypotheses.falsifier: A simpler grammar-only closed relation set covers the frozen/general-purpose language without extensibility loss, or typed relation resolution adds avoidable ambiguity/cost without benefit.

hypotheses.claim: Allowing bare identifier-like infix relations is superior to lexically explicit relation marking.
counterevidence: strict generic quoted-call candidate also removes relation vocabulary from lexer/operator classification
hypotheses.falsifier: A declared contextual-infix implementation parses the complete corpus with stable AST, precise typo diagnostics, equal semantic-hash preservation and lower measured reader/token/repair cost than both strict candidates.

hypotheses.claim: The production BASE relation surface should be selected by a three-way executable comparison: sigil-hybrid vs strict generic quoted-call vs declared contextual bare-infix, rather than by syntax preference.
hypotheses.falsifier: One candidate fails basic full-corpus semantic preservation before a three-way cost/diagnostic comparison is meaningful.

negative_results.claim: Bare open relation words are not safe to freeze without an explicit lexical+semantic resolution policy; prior E2B replication exposed an identifier-vs-relation ambiguity.
Neither the sigil-hybrid nor the strict generic quoted-call candidate is justified for promotion from local proxy/fuzz evidence alone; full-corpus and reader/repair measurements remain required.
